decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1.75%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1 3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-3/4 percent.”

changes.quote: The information that has become available since the last meeting of the Committee confirms that economic activity has been receiving considerable upward impetus from a marked swing in inventory investment.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The information that has become available since the last meeting of the Committee indicates that the economy, bolstered by a marked swing in inventory investment, is expanding at a significant pace.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: In these circumstances, although the stance of monetary policy is currently accommodative, the Committee believes that, for the foreseeable future, against the background of its long run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are balanced with respect to the prospects for both goals.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.62% APR costs about $56.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.09% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.88% would fall by about $2.00 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.9%, and employers added an average of -81k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.6% over the past year (April 2002); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced.
